consent.title: Usage statistics
consent.body: This site can send anonymous usage statistics to GameAnalytics and Google Analytics: which screens and actions are used, how seasons go and how money moves. It never sends names, your garage or your saves. Nothing is sent or stored unless you accept, and you can change your mind at any time.

mobile.body: Last Combustion is a management game with dense tables and panels, built for a desktop or laptop with a mouse and a large screen. It will not work well on a phone or a tablet.

shell.gettingStarted: Your first season starts with the first prelims. Before you run them:
shell.start.sponsor: Sign a title sponsor in Sponsors, so money comes in as well as going out.
shell.start.staff: Hire a mechanic in Staff: a crew cuts part wear and repair bills.
shell.start.drivers: Check your driver and car in Drivers and Cars, and look for a better fit.
shell.start.run: Then press Continue to skip to the first prelims, and again to run them.
about.title: About
about.describe1: The Last Combustion of the Petrol Engine, or Last Combustion for short, is a racing management game set in a post-petrol world. In 2031 the last petrolheads race road-legal combustion cars on closed Australian public roads, in a series that scores every driver in a field of over three hundred.
about.describe2: You run a garage. Buy and upgrade cars, sign drivers, hire a crew and executives, and deal with sponsors and suppliers, then race six rounds a season and try to build a name that lasts. Drivers grow, retire and are replaced, garages rise and fold, and every season you finish begins the next.
about.describe0: Dwarf Fortress meets MF Ghost meets Aussie car culture.
about.describe3: Nothing is forgotten. Every driver, car, garage, prelim and race has a profile in the Registry, and the Almanac keeps the champions, the awards and the records.
about.creditsIntro: Last Combustion stands on other people's work. These are the third-party assets and data it uses, each with its licence.
about.fiction: Last Combustion is a work of fiction. The manufacturers, cars, sponsors, suppliers, garages, drivers, executives, journalists and every other character are invented, and any resemblance to real people, living or dead, or to real companies, products, brands or events is purely coincidental. Names are made up from lists and may by chance match a real person's. Real towns and roads are used only to set the scene. No real person, brand or organisation has endorsed this game or has any connection with it.

daily.title: Daily life
daily.intro: On the days between rounds the cars are driven on everyday and delivery roads. That earns delivery pay for the garage (more in a busy area, set by where the driver lives), wears the car and its parts a little, and slowly trains the driver on the kind of road around their home. A driver can move home in the off-season.

ownership.raise.explain: Sell new preferred shares to an investor. They get the share of the garage that their money is worth to them, which dilutes every holder. One round a year.

investments.takeover.explain: Bid a premium over the garage's worth. Every holder whose asking premium is at or below your bid accepts. If the acceptors and your own shares hold over half the votes, the bid carries and everyone else is bought out at the same price, from your garage's cash. Its cars, its driver contracts that run on, its fans and its cash become yours, and it closes. Only between seasons.

entries.title: Entries
entries.intro: An entry is one car and one driver. Each extra entry costs up to about {cost} a round in fees, tyres, servicing and travel. Entries can be changed until the season starts.
entries.full: The garage has as many entries as it is allowed.
entries.needCar: To add an entry you need a spare car that is not racing.
entries.needDriver: To add an entry you need a signed driver who is not racing. Sign one in the Drivers panel.
dealer.heading: Dealers
dealer.newIntro: Every model on sale this year, at the list price less any deal your garage has with the manufacturer.
dealer.sellIntro: A dealer pays a share of a car's value and lists it on the used market for more. A car with an entry this season cannot be sold.
dealer.nothingToSell: You have no car to sell that is not racing.
auction.heading: Auctions
auction.none: There is no auction open. The next one opens after the next round.
auction.intro: Name the most you will pay for a lot. The auction raises your bid only as far as it must to beat the others, so you pay one step over the second best bid, never more than your maximum. The buyer pays {premium}% on top and a seller loses {fee}%. The auction closes after the next round, and a lot under its reserve goes unsold.

staff.intro: Mechanics look after the cars. A good crew saves wear on parts and the cost of crash repairs, and every mechanic is paid each round.
staff.explain: A full crew is one expert mechanic for each of your {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}: skill counts, so two average mechanics cover one expert. Notice costs a round's wages.
staff.none: You employ no mechanics, so the cars are looked after by the owner.
